sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Retail of Oversized Furniture and Home Decor

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Civil Law for private matters under the Civil Code of Québec; Common Law for federal public and criminal matters; federal-state division of powers)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: CPTPP (Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership, in force for Canada 2018)
CETA (Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement, provisionally applied 2017)
Canada-China Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (FIPA, in force October 1, 2014)
Hague Apostille Convention (acceded by Canada; effective January 11, 2024)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17 (PCMLTFA) and FINTRAC Regulations; Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46, ss. 462.3–462.5; Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17; United Nations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. U-2; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, S.C. 2011, c. 31. Provincial (Quebec): An Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, ss. 16.1–16.17 (beneficial ownership disclosure to the Registraire des entreprises du Québec); Regulation respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, r. 1.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport or government-issued photo identification for every general partner and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or commissioner of oaths in the document's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (effective in Canada since January 11, 2024) OR Consular Legalization where the origin state is not an Apostille Convention party

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing / corporate register extract (for any corporate general partner or corporate limited partner)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry of the foreign partner's jurisdiction of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original notarized declaration of partnership (déclaration de société en commandite) and UBO identification schedule
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Quebec notary (notaire en exercice) or licensed attorney attesting under the Civil Code of Québec
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic notarization (no apostille required for documents issued within Canada)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police / criminal record certificate (RCMP security clearance or equivalent) for every general partner and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Royal Canadian Mounted Police or accredited local police authority in the individual's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for foreign-issued certificates; directly filed for Canadian-issued certificates

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-closing screening of every general partner, limited partner above the 25% threshold, and all ultimate beneficial owners against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, Global Affairs Canada sanctions lists (Special Economic Measures Act and United Nations Act schedules), the U.S. OFAC SDN and consolidated non-SDN lists, and FINTRAC-endorsed watchlists. Enhanced due diligence and senior-approval sign-off are required for all foreign and domestic politically exposed persons (PEPs), their family members, and close associates as defined under the PCMLTFA regulations. Any positive match, latent risk indicator, or suspicious transaction observation must be escalated for a suspicious transaction report (STR) to FINTRAC prior to incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Québec Enterprise Register) — online services at https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Charter of the French Language, CQLR c. C-11: the Quebec limited partnership name filed under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises must be in French or must otherwise satisfy the statutory francisation rules; the legal designation must include the French form 'société en commandite' or the abbreviation 'S.E.C.'. A transliterated or non-French trade name is admissible only where the name also contains a French element, a recognized trademark exemption applies, or ministerial authorization is obtained; French must have clear visual preponderance on all signage, invoices, and e-commerce materials in Quebec.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: 'Bank', 'banque', 'Trust', 'Insurance', 'Assurance' — require prior approval of the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF)
'Royal', 'Crown', 'Police', 'Gendarmerie' — restricted tokens requiring ministerial or Crown consent
'Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Ltd.', 'Limited', 'Corporation' — misleading corporate endings incompatible with limited partnership status
Words contrary to public order, obscene terms, or names implying a criminal or quasi-criminal enterprise
Third-party trademarks or trade names absent written authorization
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon refusal (avis de refus), the filer may submit, within 30 days of the notice date, a written request for review (demande de révision) to the Legal Affairs Directorate of the Registraire des entreprises du Québec, attaching a revised proposed name, a legal justification memorandum, and any supporting trademark or authorization evidence. The Registrar must reconsider the file and issue a new decision within 30 days. A confirmed refusal may be contested by judicial review before the Superior Court of Québec under the Québec Code of Civil Procedure. In parallel, the filer is advised to reserve an alternative distinctive French-language name and proceed with the registration to avoid delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for statutory registration purposes only if the virtual office provider supplies a physical commercial street address in Quebec, mail-forwarding, and a reception service, and that address is declared as the establishment address in the LP's declaration filed with the Registraire des entreprises. However, payment processors (Stripe, Affirm BNPL) and regulated financial institutions will typically require evidence of a physical operating address, warehouse, or fulfillment facility for the oversized furniture e-commerce activity; a purely virtual registered office without commercial substance may trigger additional KYC scrutiny or account holds.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate: approximately 5% annual probability of an unannounced verification visit or correspondence-based verification by the Registraire des entreprises for a standard serviced-office address; the likelihood rises to 15–25% if a residential or shared coworking address is declared, if consumer complaints under Quebec consumer protection law are filed, or if the declared establishment cannot demonstrate any tangible commercial activity.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name reservation (réservation de nom) filed online with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec, valid 90 days
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the Regulation respecting the fees payable under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, r. 1 (approximately CAD 45 online)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Initial registration of the société en commandite (Limited Partnership) declaration and issuance of the certificate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff, approximately CAD 85, as amended by the applicable REQ fee regulation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and legal drafting of the partnership declaration, UBO identification schedule, and statutory consent resolutions by a Quebec notary
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing Quebec market benchmark for LP constitutive documentation and UBO schedules

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille or consular legalization of foreign identity and corporate records for an estimated 3–4 partners/UBOs
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Global Affairs Canada Authentication sector and consular authorities of origin states
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Canadian statutory authentication fee of CAD 15 per document plus foreign consular fees and courier; average USD 125–150 per bundle

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP, OFAC, UN, and domestic sanctions screening via FINTRAC-compliant commercial database (one-time pre-closing sweep)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate for automated AML/CFT screening and continuous monitoring setup

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Police / criminal record certificate verification (RCMP or accredited local authority) for general partners and UBOs
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Royal Canadian Mounted Police / local police authority
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory RCMP vulnerable-sector verification fee and accredited agency processing fees

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and commercial mail-forwarding arrangement at a physical Quebec street address (three-month initial term)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Serviced office / registered office provider in Quebec
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing Quebec market benchmark for virtual office and registered establishment address services

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec, CQLR c CCQ-1991, arts. 2186-2188, 2236-2266 (société en commandite); An Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, ss. 8-17, 33-36; Regulation respecting the application of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c P-44.1, r. 1)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), Directorate of Enterprise Registration, Ministère de la Justice du Québec
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration de société en commandite (Declaration of Limited Partnership) filed electronically through the REQ transactional portal 'clicSÉQUR'; optional preliminary name reservation under the enterprise name rules of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum statutory capital and no escrow account requirement. The general partner has unlimited liability; each limited partner's liability is limited to its stated contribution (apport), which must be recorded in the declaration. Contributions may be in cash, property, or services, but services do not create limited-liability protection; capital schedules must be annexed to the partnership agreement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, by the General Partner of the Partnership, acting as managing body: (1) The Partnership Agreement (contrat de société en commandite) dated [DATE] and the execution copy of the Declaration of Limited Partnership to be filed with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec are approved and adopted in their entirety. (2) The registered office shall be located at 1250 Boulevard René-Lévesque Ouest, Suite 2200, Montréal, Québec, H3B 4W8, Canada. (3) Laurent Gagnon is appointed General Partner Manager with delegated authority to open banking accounts, execute Stripe and Affirm merchant agreements, and engage legal counsel for municipal, environmental, and CNESST licensing. (4) All limited partners' contributions are acknowledged as received and recorded in the capital schedule. (5) The Manager is authorized to implement this resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – online name reservation module (clicSÉQUR)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed partnership name in French or bilingual form, including the mandatory legal designation 'société en commandite' or 'S.E.C.'; the system performs the distinguishability search against the enterprise register and generates a reservation certificate valid for 90 days; an English-only trade name is permissible only with the French legal designation.
required_dossiers: Completed online name reservation application
Consent letter of each proposed general partner to the proposed name
Power of attorney or authorization of the filer if an agent files on behalf of the partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If refused for non-distinguishability, file a new request adding a distinctive element or obtain written consent of the earlier-name holder; judicial remedy is available before the Court of Québec within 60 days of REQ refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Limited Partnership Agreement and Capital Contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Independent Québec notary or licensed business lawyer acting for the partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the French-language contrat de société en commandite before a notary or attorney; document each limited partner's contribution in cash or in-kind, the allocation of profits and losses, transfer restrictions, withdrawal rights, manager mandate, and dissolution events; each corporate partner must attach its own board consent; the agreement must be bilingual if any partner requests it.
required_dossiers: Draft partnership agreement (contrat de société en commandite)
Schedule of capital contributions with valuation of in-kind assets
Consents and corporate resolutions of any corporate general or limited partner
Identification and KYC dossiers of each partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a drafting defect is identified by the notary, counsel, or REQ, execute an amending private deed (avenant) and re-attest; no regulatory penalty attaches if the amendment is filed as a rectifying declaration within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Initial Declaration of Limited Partnership and Official Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (clicSÉQUR transactional portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Sign and transmit the initial declaration of limited partnership online, stipulating the registered office in Québec, full identification of the general partner, each limited partner's name and contribution, the partnership's duration, and winding-up provisions; pay the applicable registration tariff via credit card, debit, or pre-authorized account; the REQ then issues the official certificate of registration and the Québec Enterprise Number (NEQ).
required_dossiers: Completed initial declaration form (P-44.1, s. 16)
Reserved name certificate, if a name reservation was obtained
Notarized or private partnership agreement in support
Payment receipt for the registration tariff
Mandate and authorization of the general partner for the filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ queries the declaration, file a correcting declaration (déclaration rectificative) online without penalty within 30 days of discovery; after that, a formal administrative correction request and Court of Québec review under s. 34 P-44.1 are available.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Quebec and Federal Tax Account Registrations (QST, GST/HST, Payroll and CNESST)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec – Direction générale de l'inscription; Canada Revenue Agency – Business Registration Online (BRO)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the NEQ is issued, register the limited partnership with Revenu Québec for Québec Sales Tax (QST/TVQ), source deductions, and the general partners' payroll accounts; concurrently request the CRA Business Number and GST/HST Program Account using the same NEQ-linked legal name; submit the manager appointment resolution as the tax representative mandate.
required_dossiers: Certificate of registration and attestation issued by REQ
Form LM-101-V (Revenu Québec inscription demande)
Form RC159 or RC1 (CRA Program Account request)
Identity, residency, and tax status records of the general partner and each limited partner
Partnership agreement and first resolution appointing the manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is delayed or queried, contact Revenu Québec and CRA via secure message (Messagerie d'affaires) with the NEQ and partnership deed; request retroactive effective dating with lease or first-sale invoices as supporting evidence; CRA objections follow a 90-day administrative review period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Permit, Zoning and Occupancy Certification for Warehouse and Head Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ville de Montréal – Service des permis et inspections (or the municipality where the fulfillment warehouse is situated)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain a certificat d'occupation (occupancy certificate) and, if applicable, a commercial exploitation permit for the head office and warehouse; verify that 'online retail warehousing and home-delivery base' is an authorized use in the zoning by-law; file the lease plan and mechanical/structural drawings for racks, mezzanines, loading docks, and fire separations under the Quebec Construction Code; pay the municipal tariff and receive the inspection appointment.
required_dossiers: Completed municipal permit application for the occupancy certificate
Lease agreement and architectural/mechanical plans of the premises
Fire-safety system contract, alarm monitoring, and fire-extinguisher purchase invoices
Structural and racking installation drawings sealed by an engineer
Proof of municipal tax payment on the premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If refused or conditioned, submit revised plans addressing fire-safety and structural comments; appeal the decision before the municipality's review committee (comité de révision) within 30 days under the Charter of Ville de Montréal, Chapter IV; interim remedial permits may be requested for non-structural corrections.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Environmental, Residual Material and Occupational Health-Safety Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MELCCFP – Direction du suivi environnemental; CNESST – dossier employeur; Éco Entreprises Québec (furniture extended producer responsibility program)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the warehouse with CNESST for workplace insurance and employer file; confirm the activity's exemption from the mandatory project EIA list under the Regulation respecting environmental impact assessment (REA) because no listed industrial process is installed; join the furniture and packaging EPR program managed in the residual materials framework; sign written waste recovery contracts covering cardboard, plastic film, wood pallets, and used batteries/oils.
required_dossiers: CNESST employer registration form (A-1/A-2)
Written declaration to MELCCFP that no listed industrial activity is undertaken
EPR adherence agreement with the furniture recovery organization (Éco Entreprises Québec or equivalent)
Copies of waste hauler permits and authorized recovery site certificates
Monthly residual-material tonnage register format
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond within 30 days to any MELCCFP notice by providing proof of compliant recovery contracts; if annual residual waste is below 1,000 kg, request a discretionary exemption; CNESST adjustment requests may be filed through the online employer portal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Governance Setup, Banking and E-commerce Payment Rail Onboarding (Stripe and Affirm)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Partner Manager; Québec-chartered bank; Stripe and Affirm underwriting compliance teams
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the General Partner management meeting and adopt the governance minutes, bank mandates, and payment-rail authorization resolution; open the partnership's bank account in the legal name; submit the REQ attestation, partnership deed, KYC forms, and beneficial-ownership certificate to Stripe and Affirm under the furniture retail merchant category code; configure payout accounts and payment dispute policies.
required_dossiers: Official extract (extrait du registre) from REQ showing the partnership's registration
Partnership agreement and first management resolution
KYC/UBO forms for each partner, including non-resident ownership declarations
Bank signatory resolution, void cheque, and authorized banking mandate
Merchant application for Stripe and Affirm with MCC 4799/5712 description for oversized furniture retail
Compliance attestation for BNPL payment disclosure rules
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the payment processor defers onboarding, submit supplementary source-of-funds schedules and current partnership financial statements; request escalation to the commercial compliance committee; if banking KYC is delayed, use a co-opted second signatory or open a bridge account with a schedule-I bank until full onboarding is complete.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Régie du bâtiment du Québec (RBQ) – Service des permis; Ville de Montréal – Service des permis et inspections, as municipal building and occupancy authority; CNESST as workplace safety regulator
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sectoral retail licence is imposed on ISIC 4791 online furniture sales (low-risk standard activity). Mandatory physical operating instruments are the municipal certificat d'occupation and commercial exploitation permit, the RBQ building permit for racking and mezzanine works, and the CNESST workplace clearance certificate for the fulfillment warehouse.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP) – Direction de l'évaluation environnementale et du suivi
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / registration-only tier: warehousing and online distribution operations appear on no listed category of the Regulation respecting environmental impact assessment (REA), so no full EIA Report is required; the partnership must nevertheless maintain self-declaration files under the residual materials regulations (REIMR) and join the furniture extended producer responsibility program.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: no industrial process water; only sanitary discharge to municipal sewers, respecting 300 mg/L BOD5 and 300 mg/L suspended solids limits of the municipal sewer by-law. Air: no coating, painting, or VOC-emitting finish is authorized inside the warehouse; propane forklift exhaust must meet CNESST occupational exposure limits; vehicle idling limited to 3 minutes. Residual waste: corrugated cardboard, plastic wrap, and wood pallets must reach at least 70% recovery under the REIMR and EPR programs; hazardous wastes (spent engine oil, batteries, aerosol residues) require hazardous-material manifests, authorized transporters, and disposal at permitted sites.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification under the Fire Safety Act (RLRQ, c. S-3.4) including sprinkler coverage for high-rack storage, fire alarm monitoring, emergency lighting, and exit signage; structural load inspection of racking and mezzanines per the Quebec Construction Code; CNESST workplace clearance covering material-handling training, personal protective equipment, manual-lifting limits for oversized furniture, and verification of loading-dock safety devices; elevator and pallet-jack certifications; insurer's warehouse inspection report accepted as supplementary occupational clearance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) for federal GST/HST; Revenu Québec (RQ) for Quebec Sales Tax (QST). Portals: CRA My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/cra-login-services.html) and Revenu Québec CliquezAffaires (https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/online-services/).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign Limited Partnership must obtain a federal GST/HST account by filing Form RC1M – Request for a Business Number (BN) with CRA, and must separately register for QST with Revenu Québec using Form LM-1-V (Application for Registration – QST). Required supporting documents include the partnership’s constituent agreement, offshore proof of legal existence, the Canadian agent/representative appointment (if non-resident), and a completed Canadian Revenue Agency Business Number questionnaire. Processing generally takes 2–8 weeks; the LP must, from the registration effective date, charge GST/HST and QST on taxable supplies made in Quebec.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not operate a US-style 'check-the-box' system. Under the Income Tax Act (sections 96–103), a Limited Partnership is fiscally transparent: income, gains, credits, and recaptures flow through to partners. For GST/HST purposes, the partnership is treated as a separate 'person' and is itself a registrant if it makes taxable supplies, with no equivalent to hybrid mismatch elections. Partners may separately elect under section 216 of the Income Tax Act for net rental income treatment only if the partnership derives solely from real property; otherwise, no pass-through election alternatives are available. No hybrid mismatch election exists under Canadian law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT/GST – Federal Goods and Services Tax (GST) at 5% plus Quebec Sales Tax (QST) at 9.975%; combined Quebec consumer-facing rate is 14.975%
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: GST/HST registration threshold: CAD 30,000 of worldwide taxable supplies from all sales in the preceding 12 months; QST registration threshold: CAD 30,000 of taxable supplies made in Quebec in the preceding 12 months. A foreign online retailer without physical presence in Canada must register as soon as Canadian/Quebec taxable supplies exceed these thresholds; there is no small-supplier exemption for non-residents supplying digital or tangible goods through electronic channels.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not currently mandate real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping for GST/HST or QST invoices. Invoices must contain mandatory tax information (transaction date, supplier/recipient identification, description, GST/QST rates and amounts, and total tax) and be preserved in French or English for six years. Electronic invoices are permitted; if used, the system must ensure integrity, readability, and auditability. Revenu Québec does not require an API-based clearance, but the CRA and RQ may request access to a filer’s electronic billing records during audit. The voluntary Pan-Canadian e-invoicing standard (Peppol BIS) is in progressive adoption but is not yet law.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Schedule VI, Part V of the Excise Tax Act, a supply of tangible personal property (e.g., oversized home furniture) is zero-rated for GST/HST purposes when the property is exported from Canada by the supplier, by the recipient, or at the direction of the supplier, and the supply is made to a person outside Canada. Goods sold online and shipped directly to a final customer outside Canada qualify for 0% GST/HST and, by reciprocal provision under Quebec’s QST regime, 0% QST, provided the supplier retains proof of exportation. Goods delivered within Canada, including to Quebec consumers, are subject to GST/HST and QST at the point-of-delivery rate; pure export transactions do not require charging tax, but the taxpayer must substantiate the physical removal from Canada within a reasonable period (normally 60 days from the time of supply).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (B13A) filed with the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) or a commercial invoice signed by the exporter when exported through a carrier
Bill of Lading or through-bill of lading issued by the ocean/air/rail carrier confirming foreign destination
Airway bill or Canada Post/USPS/private courier waybill showing Canadian pick-up and overseas delivery
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank transfer record evidencing foreign currency payment from the overseas buyer
COO (Certificate of Origin) or any certificate issued by CBSA when required
Sales contract or purchase order containing Incoterms proving the risk transfer and export responsibility
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec apply strict audit scrutiny to export zero-rating claims. If export substantiation is insufficient or the goods are subsequently diverted back into Canada or consumed in Canada, the zero-rating is reversed, GST/HST and QST become due with interest, and penalties may apply under sections 280 and 285 of the Excise Tax Act and the QST Act. Reassessments can be issued within 4 years (no time limit in cases of willful misrepresentation or fraud). Penalties include a minimum of CAD 250, plus 25% of the net tax deficiency for knowingly making false statements, gross negligence penalties of up to 50% of the tax claimed, and criminal liability for fraudulent intentions, including fines and imprisonment. For QST, Revenu Québec mirrors federal penalties and may also impose a 10% late-filing penalty plus 0.5% per month of unreported QST.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% at entity level (fiscally transparent limited partnership). Allocated net income taxed in the hands of partners: combined federal and Quebec general corporate rate 26.5% (15% federal + 11.5% Quebec); top combined individual marginal rate 53.31%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No entity-level statutory tax holiday. Eligible Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) partners may access the federal small business deduction (9% federal on first CAD 500,000 of active business income) and the Quebec reduced rate (3.2% on first CAD 500,000), producing an approximate combined rate of 12.2% for qualified active business income. Accelerated capital cost allowance (CCA) measures under the 2024 federal budget and immediate expensing provisions may reduce taxable allocations; sales tax input tax credits (GST and QST) are available to the partnership on business inputs.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T5013 Summary and T5013 Supplementary (Statement of Partnership Income) — filed with the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) through My Business Account / EDI electronic file transfer.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due no later than 5 months after the partnership fiscal period end (e.g., May 31 for a December 31 fiscal year-end). Non-resident partners must receive their T5013 slip by this same deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partnership legal name, Business Number (BN), registered address, fiscal period end date, and any Quebec establishment indicator.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Indicate the jurisdiction of each non-resident partner; enter the non-resident partner's country code and foreign tax identification number; attach the schedule of non-resident partners.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 100 / Sales, commissions and receipts from services
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from online sale of oversized furniture and home decor, including Stripe card settlements and Affirm BNPL proceeds, net of returns, allowances, and GST/QST collected as trust amounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the full partnership gross revenue regardless of partner residency; sales taxes must not be included in revenue; returns and chargebacks must be separately reconciled against the Stripe/Affirm settlement records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Rental income from any sublease of warehouse or storage space; enter 0 if not applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If a non-resident partner owns the warehouse and the LP pays rent, treat as a reportable non-arm's length transaction and prepare transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest from operating bank accounts, foreign exchange gains, supplier rebates, or government subsidies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest allocated to a non-resident partner may be subject to Part XIII withholding under deemed-dividend treatment; disclose the amount separately.
Ensure consistency with the partnership's bank statements, Stripe payouts, and Affirm settlement reports; CRA e-commerce audit algorithms cross-check payment provider data.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold (furniture acquisition and inbound freight), white-glove delivery and third-party logistics, warehouse storage, advertising and marketing, payment processing fees (Stripe), BNPL discount fees (Affirm), professional fees, insurance, and administrative expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses paid to non-arm's length non-residents (e.g., a foreign sourcing affiliate) require a transfer pricing memorandum and Form T106 reporting when the annual aggregate exceeds CAD 1,000,000.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 200 / Net income (loss) for the fiscal period
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income or loss after all allowable deductions, computed on a commercial basis and reconciled to the partners' adjusted cost base balances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The allocated net income of a non-resident limited partner is statutorily deemed a dividend under ITA s. 212(1.1) and is subject to Part XIII withholding unless the non-resident files a net-basis return under s. 216(1).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Percentage interest, allocation of income/loss, reserve adjustments, and each partner's share reported on the T5013 Supplementary slip.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For each non-resident partner, state the country of residence, treaty article claimed, and the withheld Part XIII amount; attach a completed Form NR301 to invoke treaty relief.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filed T5013: CAD 25 per day up to CAD 2,500; failure to file within three years of the deadline triggers forced late filing and a penalty equal to the greater of CAD 100 and 8% of the total of certain balances. Knowingly false filings attract a 50% gross-negligence penalty (s. 163(2)) and criminal prosecution under s. 239.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: CO-511 (Société de personnes — Déclaration de renseignements) and RL-15 (Relevé 15) — filed with Revenu Québec via the Revenu Québec electronic transmission service.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 6 months after the fiscal year-end (e.g., June 30 for a December 31 fiscal year-end, as accepted practice); RL-15 slips must be furnished to partners and to Revenu Québec by the general RL slip deadline following the calendar year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec enterprise number, partnership name, legal form (LP), fiscal period covered.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A partnership carrying on business in Quebec is required to hold an active Quebec registration; non-resident partners are taxable in Quebec to the extent the partnership has a Quebec establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec-source gross revenue from e-commerce furniture sales, including sales to Quebec consumers delivered to Quebec addresses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Revenu Québec applies the same sourcing rules as the CRA; revenue is allocated to Quebec based on the partnership's permanent establishment in Quebec.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses on a basis harmonized with the federal T5013, including COGS, delivery, logistics, storage, marketing, payment processing fees, and financing discounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-arm's length expenses paid to non-residents must satisfy Quebec's transfer pricing provision (Tax Administration Act, s. 23.0.1) and be supported by contemporaneous documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income or loss after Quebec-specific adjustments, including the Quebec capital tax allowance and investment tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The allocated Quebec net income of a non-resident partner is subject to Quebec income tax; Revenu Québec may require withholding at source on remittances to non-resident partners.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of net income/loss to each partner and issuance of RL-15 slips showing the partner's share of Quebec source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must receive an RL-15 and will file a Quebec return; the LP should retain a Quebec tax treaty reduction form where applicable.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file the CO-511 attracts penalties under the Quebec Tax Administration Act (TAA), generally CAD 25 per day up to CAD 2,500; failure to issue RL-15 slips attracts a penalty of CAD 25 per slip (minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500); unpaid Quebec tax bears daily compound interest at the prescribed rate.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% Part XIII withholding tax on distributions and allocations to non-resident partners, statutorily deemed dividends under ITA s. 212(1.1); the same 25% applies to ordinary Canadian-source dividends paid by a corporation to non-residents. Treaty relief may reduce the rate (e.g., Canada-US Treaty Article X: 15% general, 5% for a company owning 10% or more of the voting shares).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The LP must withhold the full 25% statutory rate unless the non-resident partner qualifies for treaty relief. Protocol: (1) obtain the partner's Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority; (2) collect a completed Form NR301 (or NR302 for individuals, NR303 for corporations) declaring residency and beneficial ownership; (3) retain the treaty-based waiver on file before remitting at the reduced rate; (4) identify the applicable treaty article and ownership threshold; (5) if the partner elects net-basis taxation, have the partner file a Canadian Part I return under s. 216(1) within the prescribed period and remit the resulting balance instead of Part XIII.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid to non-residents: 25% Part XIII statutory; Canada-US Treaty Article XII generally 10%, with 0% for defined cultural and software copyright royalties. Interest: 25% statutory only for participating or non-arm's length debt; arm's length interest paid to non-residents is exempt from Part XIII under domestic law; Canada-US Treaty Article XI reduces the rate to 10% (0% for arm's length interest). The LP must report all cross-border payments on Form T106.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1,000,000 aggregate value of reportable controlled transactions with non-arm's length non-residents during the fiscal year — this mandatory threshold triggers the filing of Form T106 (Information Return on Transactions with Non-Residents) and the preparation of contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation (a functional and economic analysis, local file, and, at group level, a recommended master file). The CRA may also require documentation for smaller transactions on a risk basis.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada has no UAE-format Economic Substance Regulations; the functional equivalent is the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (ITA s. 245), the transfer pricing recharacterization power under s. 247(2), and the judge-made substance-over-form doctrine. The LP must maintain real economic presence in Quebec (inventory, contracts, fulfillment operations, management decisions); a paper-only LP whose profits are allocated to a foreign partner without local substance is vulnerable to GAAR, permanent establishment attribution, and denial of treaty benefits under the limitation-on-benefits provisions of the Canada-US treaty.
